pr_body:
Update the API for the CSIS server and client.

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/41591
pr_comments: @jhedberg @alwa-nordic Any chance you guys can take a look at this, so we have a chance to get it merged before Friday?

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Add public API to CSIP/CSIS
issue_context.body: Add a public API for the Coordinated Set identification Service server and client.

review_comments:
This may be a suitable place to try to explain the problems I have with naming.
To me, an "array of set members" (like it is used in this function) sounds like a set (a number of devices that belong together).
However, the set members each contain an "array of sets", and a set (of that kind) is really a "set membership" (?)
I'll probably get it with time, but I think it is possible to find better naming.

Could the lowest level (bt_csis_client_set) be called e.g. "set_info" to indicate that this is information about a set the device is a member of (rather than a set)?
The next level (_set_member) could be kept as is (I believe this is the information for one device, containing information about the device is a member of).
The top level (array of set members) could then be called a set.

It would also help if we could (here) use "set" only for the noun, and not for the verb.

Or possibly the lowest lever could be a "set_membership"?
Then a set would be an array of "set_member"s, which would each have a number of "set_memberships".

> It would also help if we could (here) use "set" only for the noun, and not for the verb.

Yeah, it would be best to avoid any form of `set_set` :D 

> To me, an "array of set members" (like it is used in this function) sounds like a set (a number of devices that belong together).

They are similar, but not the same. 
A set may consist of 3 devices {SM_1, SM_2, SM_3}, but an array of set members could be a single set member [SM_1] or some [SM_1, SM_2] or all [SM_1, SM_2, SM_3]. 

Likewise, there may also be two sets: {SM_1, SM_2} and {SM_2, SM_3}, i.e. SM_2 is part of multiple sets, and as such must have multiple CSIS instances.  

I agree that `bt_csis_client_set` is not the optimal naming, as it really a representation of a remote CSIS instance, and not a set.  `bt_csis_client_set_info` seem to be a better choice indeed, but it is also contains more than information, so that is not optimal either in my opinion. Perhaps something like `bt_csis_client_inst`?

I see your point that the array may be only a partial set.  So it may not be correct to call the array for a set.

As for the second point, I see that my comment was lacking some words - I agree that at set_member (?) may be a member of several sets.

Your proposal for naming (`bt_csis_client_inst`) is an improvement over the current naming - I would be satisfied with that.

Hmm, `bt_csis_client_inst` is already used internally in csis_client.c, so that won't work :D 

Basically we have 
a) A set (2 or more set members)
b) An array of set members (1 or more set members)
c) A client instance to a remote server (`bt_csis_client_inst`)
d) A reference to a specific CSIS instance on a remote server (currently `bt_csis_client_set`). 

Any other suggestions for d)? I briefly considered `bt_csis_client_csis_inst` as that is the most descriptive, but that also has `csis` twice :P

I can live with that - we have seen worse before.  I find it better than calling the CSIS-instance a "set".

TheCSIS instance contains the SIRK, the set size and the rank of a device (plus an internal member), and there is one such instance for each set the device is a member of.  It could also possibly be called a "membership".  (In which case a set member will end up with several memberships, which seems OK.)

I'll update the PR with `bt_csis_client_csis_inst`. 

If we ever rename the API to follow the roles instead, it would become something like `bt_set_coordinator_csis_inst` or possibly `bt_set_coord_csis_inst` which would avoid the douple `csis`.

do we need to read it always? Don't we register for the notifications and maintain the current lock state?

So in fact, we need to read it once, after bonding, and then we should rely on notifications if we are bonded.
If not bonded, that read it only once after reconnection, and then rely on the notifications.

As per the commit message, bt_csis_client_get_lock_state is basically the ordered access procedure, which reads the lock state on a set of devices to verify that they are unlocked. This is used by e.g. CAP as an alternative for locking. 

So the question is whether we should directly expose an API for the Ordered Access Procedure, or ensure that the state is read during discovery (which would be an implicit implementation of the procedure, except that notifications are still considered unreliable). 

Given that there is no qualification test (as far as I can tell), we don't need an explicit API for this procedure. 

**So can we always just rely on notifications, or should we expose an API to read the value(s)?**
Notifications on ATT are not reliable.  It seems to follow that one should not rely upon them ;-)

> Notifications on ATT are not reliable. It seems to follow that one should not rely upon them ;-)

**unreliable** is really the keyword to consider when determining if you should **rely** on it indeed :D
